abstract: FactSet Earnings Insight report by John Butters, published June 12, 2026, giving the final full-season count of S&P 500 earnings calls citing the term "AI" for the Q1 2026 reporting period (calls conducted March 15 through June 11, 2026). The term was cited on 337 calls, representing 68% of the 498 calls conducted — the highest number in over 10 years. This supersedes FactSet's May 8, 2026 in-season update, which reported approximately 65% when only 89% of the index had reported.
keyFindings: "AI" was cited on 337 S&P 500 earnings calls during the Q1 2026 reporting period — the highest count in over 10 years
That is 68% (337 out of 498) of all S&P 500 earnings calls conducted in the period
Well above the 5-year average of 164 calls and the 10-year average of 103 calls
The prior record was Q4 2025 at 334 calls (331 of 485 companies, 68%)
On finals, Q4 2025 to Q1 2026 is essentially flat — the apparent 68→65 sequential decline seen in the May interim was an artifact of comparing an interim against a final
methodology: FactSet searches S&P 500 earnings call transcripts for the term "AI" and counts the number of calls on which it appears at least once, then expresses that as a share of all S&P 500 calls conducted within the reporting period. The Q1 2026 period runs March 15 through June 11, 2026. FactSet publishes interim counts during the reporting season and a definitive count once effectively all companies have reported; only the latter is a final.
qualifiers: Keyword-frequency measure — a single passing mention counts the same as a substantive discussion of AI strategy, and the measure cannot distinguish AI as a product line from AI as an internal workforce or efficiency initiative. The denominator varies by quarter (498 calls in Q1 2026 vs 485 in Q4 2025) because not every S&P 500 constituent holds a call within the window. Interim in-season readings are not comparable to finals and should not be plotted alongside them.
